curation.description: Analyst comparisons of explicitly registered, approved public Legacy interviews. Publication consent is not approval of these interpretations. Speaker statements, editorial omissions, contract obligations and research links remain distinct. No private account is evidence. All findings remain pending_validation.

bindings.explanation: An exactly representable monetary result must be preserved; losing significant digits is not an implicit rounding policy.
Finite exact base-10 amounts supply the relevant value-preservation boundary, not a storage-column format.
Internal storage choices remain consumer choices only while observable semantics are preserved.
Unsupported amounts fail without a Money result; the interview does not establish a portable supported-range threshold.

mappings.claim: Preserve the magnitude of a financial value; do not silently truncate it
mappings.conditions_and_limits: This is a personal recollection, not a verified experiment or a universal statement about COBOL. No details from the withheld follow-up are used. Exact representability does not define universal database field capacity. The Open Questions in spec/money/representation.md leave portable precision, scale and overflow limits unresolved: this behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core. Unsupported amounts already have a portable failure category; this comparison does not set the capacity threshold or introduce an overflow code.

evidence.exact_quote: you lose the millions, not the pence.
evidence.heading: 3. Do you remember any strange rules, unusual code, or unexpected situations that taught you something important? Especially things that might look unnecessary today but had a very good reason to exist.

mappings.interpretation: The publicly reported numeric-field incident illustrates financial damage from losing significant digits, distinct from deliberate rounding. The connection to FinKore is the analyst's interpretation, not an assertion that the interview established its decimal contract.
mappings.learn_angle: Explain why silent loss of high-order digits is different from an explicit rounding decision, and ask consumers to document their supported value profile without claiming a universal FinKore maximum digit count.

related_research.explanation: Both discussions separate exact value preservation from a universal currency-wide calculation scale; the interview supplies operational context, not experimental corroboration.

bindings.explanation: A rejected financial action preserves relevant observable financial state unless a governing rule explicitly defines another failure effect.
Failed Money operations preserve every operand; negative acceptance artifacts can inspect before/after values.
A rejected Transition leaves current State unchanged; this is a bounded example rather than a general promise of operational recovery.

mappings.claim: Treat overlooked exceptions as failure cases worth making observable
mappings.conditions_and_limits: The surrounding prediction about the first day of go-live is personal rhetoric, not a measured rate or universal temporal claim. Only failures already defined by the owning specification can acquire expected observations; a test suite must not invent banking exceptions or imply exhaustive correctness.

evidence.exact_quote: Bank’s back-end systems are full of exception handling,
evidence.heading: 4. Have you ever been involved in replacing or modernizing an old financial system? What were the biggest challenges, and what lessons did you take away?

mappings.interpretation: The interview motivates careful negative and boundary examples. A concrete failed-operation example should inspect both the error and preserved state, instead of treating an exception label as the entire outcome.
mappings.learn_angle: Introduce failure-oriented examples that show what must remain unchanged as well as the reported error, and explain why a finite fixture suite cannot enumerate every operational incident.

related_research.explanation: Failure examples have a bounded evidential scope; neither published cases nor an interview establish exhaustive implementation correctness.

bindings.explanation: Non-mutation on rejection does not restore a deployment or undo previously committed external effects.
One observable domain transition does not specify database isolation, deployment recovery, or distributed atomic commit.
Workflow preconditions explicitly do not provide distributed coordination or transaction isolation.

mappings.claim: A deployment rollback plan and a rejected-operation guarantee have different boundaries
mappings.conditions_and_limits: The interviewee frames this as advice, not a reported deployment protocol or proof of atomic recovery. Deployment rollback, external compensation, restoration of a committed action and local non-mutation on rejection are distinct. FinKore does not supply a rollback engine, distributed transaction protocol, migration workflow, or concrete reversal accounting effects.

evidence.exact_quote: a proven rollback plan before attempting any go live.
evidence.heading: 4. Have you ever been involved in replacing or modernizing an old financial system? What were the biggest challenges, and what lessons did you take away?

mappings.interpretation: The recommendation concerns operational preparation for replacing part of a running system. It helps explain why a consumer still needs migration and recovery procedures even when individual FinKore operations preserve state on rejection.
mappings.learn_angle: Discuss rejected actions versus system rollout recovery; direct readers to consumer-owned operational policy without deriving a new Core operation.

related_research.explanation: The existing compensation discussion is pending evidence. It flags different failure boundaries; it is not ready source corroboration for a recovery guarantee.

bindings.explanation: A stable category makes a domain failure recognizable across consumer environments.
The portable code must not embed localized prose or implementation details; diagnostics are separate.
Human-readable messages and structured context are permitted, not universally required.
Additional details must not expose sensitive information by default, even when troubleshooting is difficult.
Stable violation identifiers are SHOULD-level guidance; do not promote them into a universal MUST.
Relevant domain paths are SHOULD-level guidance; preserve published coverage limitations.

mappings.claim: Stable portable failures and actionable diagnostics serve different readers
mappings.conditions_and_limits: The quote is advice supported by a personal incident, not a FinKore requirement for log content, manuals, localized wording, or an error envelope. SPEC-ERROR-003 permits messages and context (MAY); entity paths and stable violation identifiers are SHOULD obligations. Sensitive financial, personal and implementation data are not automatically safe to include.

evidence.exact_quote: give enough information in the error (or log) so the poor on-call developer can trace it.
evidence.heading: 5. After all these years, what's the one thing you think the next generation of financial software developers should never forget?

mappings.interpretation: The public troubleshooting account illustrates the value of stable domain failure categories together with useful, safe optional context. Human remediation advice belongs to a consumer interface and must not change the portable category.
mappings.learn_angle: Explain how the same portable code can support localized guidance and useful domain paths without making wording portable or exposing sensitive data by default.

related_research.explanation: The related academic diagnostic discussion remains pending evidence; it does not independently validate the practitioner account or require identical diagnostic formats.

bindings.explanation: Evaluate the complete proposed result and declared relevant facts before a change becomes observable.
All structural and business rules applicable to the current State apply, not an assumed universal application schema.
Cross-field rules inspect the complete proposed domain result.
Import validates the complete supplied observation and must not bypass declared validators simply because no Mutation is proposed.

mappings.claim: Validate supplied financial observations without confusing validity with factual truth
mappings.conditions_and_limits: Product-specific names, address formats and numeric-field rules must be declared by a composing domain. The anecdote supplies no universal input grammar or guarantee that a validator detects fraud, missing facts, or all bad assumptions. FinKore validates declared conditions against supplied observations; it does not certify their real-world truth.

evidence.exact_quote: if your assumptions are wrong, or your data is rubbish, so is what you’ve built.
evidence.heading: 5. After all these years, what's the one thing you think the next generation of financial software developers should never forget?

mappings.interpretation: The warning helps explain structural validation, business validation and evaluation of the complete proposed result, including import. A supplied fact or a successful schema check does not prove that it correctly describes the external world.
mappings.learn_angle: Show the difference between well-formed input, a complete business-valid proposal and trustworthy external facts, including an example where valid structure is insufficient.

related_research.explanation: Both discussions distinguish observing or capturing input from satisfying business rules; source types and evidence strengths remain distinct.

bindings.explanation: Rejecting an already committed Audit Event identity prevents another committed event for that identity; it does not deduplicate a payment instruction.
Local expected-state/revision checks are not locks or distributed coordination for concurrent batch work.

mappings.claim: Retrying a batch is not evidence that each economic effect occurs only once
mappings.conditions_and_limits: This is a reported operational tendency, not proof that every retry duplicates payments. A retry after an uncertain outcome, a domain rejection and a new economic instruction are different cases. Concrete payment posting, batch scheduling, reconciliation and distributed effect coordination are outside the current Core contract. No idempotency key scheme, retention period or payment operation is prescribed.

evidence.exact_quote: run it all again (which causes likely duplication of payments)
evidence.heading: About legacy banking systems: Is there a particular business rule or exception-handling scenario you've encountered that you believe modern developers would probably overlook if they were building a financial system from scratch?

mappings.interpretation: The practitioner warning highlights the need to identify the retried unit and already committed effects. Duplicate audit-event rejection and workflow preconditions have bounded meanings; neither is a payment-processing guarantee.
mappings.learn_angle: Discuss request identity, committed-event identity and economic-effect identity separately, using batch retries as a practical question rather than claiming exactly-once payments.

related_research.explanation: The request-identity discussion asks about content and effect boundaries rather than assuming all retried instructions are interchangeable.
Producer idempotence and application-effect uniqueness are separate claims; no duplicate-payment guarantee is inferred from their shared topic.

bindings.explanation: Relevant external-fact dependencies must be identified for reproducible evaluation; this does not define a data-age policy.
A guard is deterministic for the same declared facts or identifies external dependencies. Retain the published PARTIAL coverage note.
Expected state/revision/conflict values are checked against the supplied observation; passing those checks does not establish remote freshness.

mappings.claim: Batch dependencies expose a distinction between reproducible facts and fresh facts
mappings.conditions_and_limits: The source supplies no quantitative freshness bound or dependency protocol. WORKFLOW-GUARD-004 does not require always-latest data; ENTITY-IMPORT-007 compares expected values to the supplied observation, not to an independently queried remote system. The interview's suggestion that real-time processing removes these problems is not generalized: distributed real-time systems still require dependency and freshness policies.

evidence.exact_quote: run against data which isn't up to date.
evidence.heading: About legacy banking systems: Is there a particular business rule or exception-handling scenario you've encountered that you believe modern developers would probably overlook if they were building a financial system from scratch?

mappings.interpretation: Downstream jobs can consume an internally coherent observation that is stale for their purpose. Declared fact dependencies make an evaluation reproducible, while source recency, completion checkpoints and permissible age require explicit consuming policy.
mappings.learn_angle: Explain supplied context, snapshot consistency and freshness as separate concerns, with explicit time/version facts where a composing domain needs them.

related_research.explanation: Response speed does not establish that the facts required for a decision are current.
Coherence of one snapshot and freshness relative to a business dependency remain separate properties.

AUDIT-APPEND-003.statement: Submission of an already committed Audit Event identity MUST fail with `FINKORE_AUDIT_DUPLICATE_EVENT` and MUST NOT create another committed event.
AUDIT-APPEND-003.title: AUDIT-APPEND-003

CORE-001.2.statement: Where a monetary calculation has an exactly representable result, it SHALL preserve that result. Precision reduction SHALL use a declared rounding rule and SHALL NOT select a rounding method or target scale implicitly.
CORE-001.2.title: Exact calculation and explicit rounding

CORE-002.2.statement: A proposed financial change SHALL be evaluated against the complete proposed result and declared relevant facts before it becomes observable. Validation or transition-condition evaluation SHALL NOT itself alter domain data.
CORE-002.2.title: Validation is complete, fact-based, and non-mutating

CORE-002.3.statement: A rejected financial action SHALL leave relevant observable financial state, financial data, and committed history unchanged, unless a governing rule expressly defines another failure effect.
CORE-002.3.title: Rejected actions have no partial financial effect

CORE-005.3.statement: For the same declared inputs, financial state, and relevant context, a financial evaluation SHALL produce the same observable outcome. A dependency on an external fact SHALL be identified when it affects that outcome.
CORE-005.3.title: Evaluation follows declared facts and context
